entries.hint: Contrastive linker used between clauses or before a command ('Ap bet!' = 'But wait!')
entries.example: Ëi xa sarpo, ap ëi kin obisëi seamenese.
entries.notes: Jorn corrected 'ap beti' -> 'ap bet*', confirming conjugated stem follows 'ap'.

entries.hint: Action of pausing or holding on ('Ap bet, beto!')

entries.notes: Conjugates regularly: Ëi=Bet, Te=Bet, Ton=Betu, Na=Betami, La=Betai, Lon=Betai.

entries.hint: Polite marker placed at the end of a request or used standalone (🙏)

entries.hint: Refers to the speaker themselves (subject/object, never possessive)

entries.hint: The expanse above the earth; combines with pan (sun) or wubu (moon)

entries.hint: This current sun-sky (et + panke)
entries.notes: Specific day/date referent; takes 3sg copula 'xaai' when used as subject.

entries.hint: Melodic sound and rhythm (🎵)

entries.hint: Core action verb of doing, making, or creating

entries.hint: Resting with eyes closed at night (😴💤)

entries.hint: Refers to the single person you are speaking to

entries.hint: Placed before a noun to show it belongs to 'Te'

entries.hint: Placed before a noun to show it belongs to 'Ton' (you all)

entries.hint: Insult used when someone is rude or makes you mibi (😠)

entries.hint: Compact in size (🤏; opposite of wo = big)
entries.notes: Antonym of wo.

entries.hint: Addressing two or more people (takes -u verb ending)
entries.notes: Plural of Te (Te + -on).

entries.hint: Positive quality, well done, or pleasant ('wo tuk' = very good!)

entries.hint: Coordinating conjunction linking words or clauses together

entries.hint: Zorpe-semen asking 'what' (triggers object fronting or copula inquiry)

entries.hint: Zorpe-semen asking the reason; keeps standard Subject-Verb-Object order after 'We'

dialogues.title: Scene 1: Panke Greetings & Energy Check
dialogues.scene: ☀️ Pan xaai in eke (Daytime). You meet your friend (buana) for the first time today.
dialogues.speaker: Buana
dialogues.seamenese: Tamako, ta buana! Etpanke xaai wo tuk panke! Wu xa te? Te xa lipo zo sarpo?
dialogues.gloss: Hello, my friend! Today is a very good day! How are you? Are you awake/energetic or tired?

options.reply: Tamako! Ëi ni xa sarpo, ëi xa wo lipo u mubu etpanke!
options.feedback: Wo tuk! You used 'ni xa sarpo' (= lipo) and the correct 1sg copula 'ëi xa'.

options.reply: Ëi xa sarpo, ap ëi kin monster u tumu, beto!
options.feedback: Tuk! 'Ap' (but) + 'ëi kin' (I need) + 'beto' (please) is completely natural Seamenese.
Watch out: 'Ta' means 'my' (possessive), and 'xaai' is for La/Lon (3rd person). Say 'Ëi xa lipo!'

dialogues.title: Scene 2: Sharing Tumu & Feeding the Silhbi
dialogues.scene: 🍽️ Lunchtime! Your friend has fish (blobber) and salad (blubur), and their small cat (ti silhbi) is watching.
dialogues.speaker: Buana
dialogues.seamenese: Ëi kin zetëi tumu! Wa te skan zetëi: blobber zo blubur? Ap bet — ta ti silhbi san kinai blobber!
dialogues.gloss: I need to eat food! What do you like to eat: fish or salad? But wait — my small cat also needs fish!

options.reply: Ëi zete blubur! Ob tëi ti silhbi blobber, beto.
options.feedback: Wo tuk! You ate the salad ('ëi zete blubur') and told your friend to give ('ob') the fish to their small cat ('tëi ti silhbi').

options.reply: Na zeteami blobber u blubur! Silhbi san zeteai!
options.feedback: Rago! You used the 1st-person plural 'Na zeteami' (we eat) and 3rd-person singular 'zeteai' for the cat.
Close! 'Zetëi' is the infinitive ('to eat'). With 'Ëi', drop -ëi and use the bare stem: 'Ëi zete blobber'.

dialogues.title: Scene 3: Learning Lulu Semen (Meta-Language Immersion)
dialogues.scene: 📖 Studying Seamenese together. Your friend wants to ask you a question (zorpe) about verbs (jai-semen) and question words (zorpe-semen).
dialogues.speaker: Buana
dialogues.seamenese: Ap bet! Ëi kin zorpei te 1 zorpe. Te pon lulu semen? Bero kiniwa: wa xaai 'jai-semen' u 'zorpe-semen'?
dialogues.gloss: But wait! I need to ask you 1 question. Do you understand the new words? Please explain: what are 'jai-semen' and 'zorpe-semen'?

options.reply: Ha, ëi pon! Jai-semen jaai ('obisëi', 'zetëi'), u zorpe-semen zorpeai ('wa', 'we', 'wu')!
options.feedback: Wo tuk kiniwako! You explained both compound nouns using pure Seamenese!

options.reply: Hani... ëi ni pon. Te kiniwa ëi, beto!
options.feedback: Natural response! Using 'Hani' (maybe) and asking your partner to explain ('Te kiniwa ëi, beto') keeps the conversation in Seamenese.

dialogues.title: Scene 4: Etwuke Vibes, Ezuki & Skantar
dialogues.scene: 🌝 Wubu xaai in eke — it is tonight (etwuke). Music (ezuki) is playing, and a group of friends (lon) are celebrating.
dialogues.speaker: Buana
dialogues.seamenese: Daka! Etwuke lon obiseai, lon skanai ezuki, u ta buana itxai lai skantar! Te rago?
dialogues.gloss: Cheers! Tonight they are talking, they like the music, and my friend kisses his/her crush! Do you agree/vibe?

options.reply: Daka! Ha, ëi rago! Etwuke na xaami wo mubu u na wo skanami ezuki!
options.feedback: Daka! You used 'na xaami' (we are) and the intensified 'wo skanami' (we love)!

options.reply: Eke mikeai u ëi xa sarpo. Taki, ta buana! Etwuke ëi sarp.
options.feedback: Great situational contrast! 'Eke mikeai' (the sky is raining) + 'ëi xa sarpo' (I am sleepy) + 'Taki' (Bye).
